subject: Clarify: data use commitments, prompt/response ownership & KMS residency
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wallace <emma.wallace@novamed.com>
Cc: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-16 09:12 -0700
Subject: Clarify: data use commitments, prompt/response ownership & KMS residency

Emma — thanks for sending the redlines. I reviewed the PDF quickly and want to clarify a few operational items before we loop legal: 

- "No adaptive training" vs "no derivatives": are you expecting an explicit prohibition on using tenant interactions to update our model weights, or do you also want restrictions on internal evaluation/metrics that might be used for model tuning?
- Ownership: you asked for exclusivity over prompts/responses. We typically grant customer rights to their prompts and generated outputs but keep aggregate telemetry for platform operations. Can you confirm whether you need assignment of IP or just a covenant not to use outputs for model improvement?
- KMS/residency: you requested keys and CME (client-managed keys) in your region. We can offer onshore KMS for an additional compliance add-on. Operationally this changes export and backup flows — will Novamed require KMS in a specific AWS region or on-prem HSM?

I attached the redlines you sent and flagged a few line items. If helpful I can loop in Legal and Ops with more concrete clause language and an operational runbook. What is your timing on procurement/DocuSign?

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novamed_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (redline), redline_comments.docx (notes)

From: Emma Wallace <emma.wallace@novamed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-10-16 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: data use commitments, prompt/response ownership & KMS residency

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick look. A few clarifications from our side: 

- High level ask: Novamed needs a contractual commitment that our customer data, including prompts and model outputs, will not be used to improve or adapt Redwood models (no adaptive training). We also want explicit ownership/custody language for generated outputs to ensure downstream licensing is controlled by Novamed.
- Telemetry: We can tolerate anonymized operational telemetry for SLO monitoring but require a documented boundary and an audit path proving telemetry cannot be used to retrain models.
- KMS: preference is US-EAST-2 (Ohio) managed by our KMS tenancy. If that isn't possible, we want on-prem HSM integration or a signed attestation of key residency and export controls.

Procurement notes: Legal will review any proposed clause language; procurement aims to finalize by Oct 29. I've attached our annotated redline (Novamed_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf).

Emma Wallace
Head of Security & Privacy
Novamed Health

Subject: Re: Clarify: data use commitments, prompt/response ownership & KMS residency

Emma / Karthik — looping in ops/legal context. Quick operational proposal to address Novamed's primary concerns: 

1) Contract language (suggested): "Provider shall not use Customer Data, including prompts and model outputs, to update or retrain Provider's production model weights or to derive model improvements for the purpose of commercializing improved models for third parties." (that gives us room to keep platform telemetry for SRE but forbids weight updates)

2) Telemetry boundary: commit to a documented telemetry contract with a definition table (what is allowed: error rates, latency, anonymized counters; what is forbidden: raw prompt text, full transcripts retained beyond ephemeral cache).

3) KMS/residency paths we can offer: 
   - Option A: Customer-managed KMS in customer's AWS account (preferred) with envelope encryption keys — requires our connector and periodic key rotation support.
   - Option B: Dedicated onshore HSM for Novamed in us-east-2 (managed by Redwood but only accessible via an audited KMS path).

4) Operational proof: provide an evidence pack (audit logs, exportable traces) and a signed attestation describing data flow and retention. We can deliver a bespoke ops runbook (attached) that maps redline lines to operational controls.

If that language looks OK from Novamed legal, David and I can craft precise redline text for the DPA and a short SOW for the onshore KMS add-on. Kim

Kim Park
Director, Product Ops (Privacy & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_ops_runbook.xlsx

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wallace <emma.wallace@novamed.com>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19 10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: data use commitments, prompt/response ownership & KMS residency

Hi all — a few practical notes from Legal/Platform: 

- Wording tweak: rather than a blanket "shall not use", we recommend the clause explicitly call out "model weights" and "model training" to avoid ambiguity around legitimate engineering activities (e.g., security research, synthetic load testing). Proposed line: 
  "Provider will not use Customer Data to perform model training, model fine-tuning, or otherwise update production model weights used to serve third-party customers; Provider may retain aggregated, non-identifiable metrics for internal service reliability and capacity planning."

- Implementation constraints: if Novamed uses customer-managed KMS (Option A), we can disable telemetry exports that contain raw text and rotate keys without retaining ciphertext keys in our control plane. Option B (Redwood-managed onshore HSM) needs an SOW and 90-day lead time for provisioning.

- Audit: we can commit to quarterly exportable audit manifests (S3 export with signed checksum) showing no-training flags, key rotations, and access logs for HSM/KMS usage. We will also support a one-time inspection by an independent auditor under NDA.

If Novamed signs off on the proposed language and confirms KMS path, I'll draft the DPA redline and an SOW for the HSM offering.

Regards,
David Kim
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

2) Please confirm lead times and cost delta for Option B (Redwood-managed onshore HSM in us-east-2). Procurement needs a line-item for budgeting.

Assuming we get that attestation and a short SOW, Legal is prepared to do a quick review and then Procurement will move to DocuSign. Target: signature by Oct 29.
